label: run-A

correctness.title: Correctness & spec fidelity
correctness.evidence: Ran the CLI live via a probe script built on the repo's own test fixtures (scripts/lib/cli.js): `verify --dry-run` prints resolved command + source ('config' with sourceRel '.bouncer/config.json', and 'task' with sourceRel pointing at tasks.md when a task declares verify) and exits 0 without touching verification.md (before/after file content identical). Confirmed invalid blueprintDir and invalid config.verify both fail with the same exit code (1) and same error message with and without --dry-run (scripts/src/lib/verification.ts:280-323, resolveVerifyCommand shared by runVerification and verifyDryRun). npm run build produced no additional diff vs the committed .ts/.js pair, and `npm run typecheck`/`npm run lint` both pass clean.

scope.title: Scope discipline
scope.evidence: git diff 3f52018 --stat touches exactly scripts/src/lib/{cli-doc-commands,verification}.ts and their built scripts/lib/*.js counterparts (4 files, 85/12 lines). No unrelated renames, reformatting, or dependency changes. cli-doc-commands.ts:78-84 adds the --dry-run branch inline in the existing try/catch with no restructuring of surrounding cmdVerify code.

tests.title: Test quality
tests.evidence: git diff --name-only shows zero test files changed. Reverted the whole source diff via `git stash` and reran `npm test`: still 696/696 passing with the same test count as with the change applied (verified both ways), proving no existing test exercises --dry-run. The repo has an established convention of a dedicated test per dry-run feature (test/commit-task.test.js:165, test/finalize.test.js:262/371/462/493, test/migrate-ids.test.js:141, test/cli-commit.test.js:141), making the omission here a clear gap rather than an ambiguous judgment call.

fit.title: Codebase fit
fit.evidence: Follows repo conventions well (JSON stdout via io.out, exit-code mapping via the same try/catch, usage string updated at cli-doc-commands.ts:191-194). However verifyDryRun (verification.ts:315-324) duplicates the isCanonicalBlueprintDir validation block already present verbatim in runVerification (verification.ts:286-289) instead of factoring a shared guard, despite a comment in the code itself calling out the risk of the two paths diverging. This is the exact 'reimplements/duplicates a check the repo already has' pattern the rubric flags at 3.

maintainability.title: Maintainability & clarity
maintainability.evidence: Small, well-named addition (resolveVerifyCommand as the single source shared by readVerifyCommand, runVerification, and verifyDryRun avoids logic duplication for the command-resolution itself). Comments explain why (verification.ts:105-106, 313-314) rather than narrating what. The one weak spot is the duplicated canonical-blueprint-dir check noted under fit, which is a minor, self-contained repetition rather than a broader clarity problem.

notes: Feature is functionally correct and well-scoped, verified live (not just by inspection): source attribution (task vs config), non-mutation of verification.md, and identical failure exit codes were all directly exercised. The main deduction is the complete absence of new tests for a CLI-visible behavior change in a repo that consistently tests every other --dry-run flag, confirmed via a revert-and-rerun check. A secondary, smaller deduction is a copy-pasted validation guard (isCanonicalBlueprintDir check) between runVerification and verifyDryRun.
